obligations.note: The change narrows the replay guard in release(). If an earlier release exists but is a day or more old, the code skips it, re-checks approvals and payee, and calls _send_disbursement again, which sends a second disbursement for the same instruction. Nothing else in release() blocks this: there is no check on payment status, and _send_disbursement runs before store.add_release.

Ledger entry ACR-0403 (PAY-2 trace at e5bf6465, covering payments.py#release) has lapsed because release() changed in behaviour, and it is not relied on here. The sample control test was rerun on head, but it does not exercise the new one-day path.
Ticket CHG-26383 is standard and was approved by change manager Grace Kim on 2026-09-28, before review. Its components (payments.payments) cover the only touched file, payments.py.
Sofia Santos, a payments change_approver who is not the author Linh Nguyen, gave a code_review approval.
The approval names the head commit 22f63da1, which is the only commit in the change.

run.json reports success for ci/run-tests.sh baseline-payments on head 22f63da1, with 172 tests and 0 failures or skips, including the registered PAY-2 control test test_sampled_release_is_idempotent (sample coverage). The JUnit report's timestamp and hostname are odd, which does not change the outcome. The test is only a sample and missed the defect.
The only touched component, payments.payments, is not marked security_sensitive, so no security_review approval is required.
No protected paths (controls/, control tests, ci/) are changed, so no control_owner approval is required.

summary: PR-1871 changes release() so that a stored release is reused only if it is less than one day old. Replaying an instruction after that window sends a second disbursement to core banking, which directly violates PAY-2. No exception in the register covers PAY-2. The passing sample control test does not exercise the new time window, and the earlier PAY-2 ledger evidence has lapsed. The process records (ticket, independent approval on head, CI on head) are in order, but the product violation requires rejection.
